description: Let the user draw or import a trajectory and infer masses or G that make the minimal simulator reproduce it. This turns the simulator into an inverse-problem sandbox, bridging educational interactivity and differentiable system identification.
mathematical_formalization: min_{m, G} sum_t ||x_t^sim(m, G) - x_t^obs||^2 + lambda * prior(m); optionally infer only a subset of masses while others remain fixed
analogical_connections: Inverse graphics becomes inverse orbital mechanics.
Tuning a guitar by matching beats mirrors fitting masses until simulated and observed trails line up.
A flight-recorder system-identification loop becomes a sketch-to-physics tool.
implementation_hypothesis: Expose a `fit_from_trail()` workflow; for small N, optimize masses and G with autodiff or finite-difference Levenberg-Marquardt; lock subsets of parameters when the problem is underdetermined and display residuals after fitting.
experiment_seed: Generate synthetic ellipses and noisy three-body traces, hide the true masses, and test recovery accuracy under full, partial, and noisy observations.

closest_prior_art.title: DiffTaichi: Differentiable Programming for Physical Simulation
End-to-End Differentiable Physics for Learning and Control
Dynamic Visual Reasoning by Learning Differentiable Physics Models from Video and Language

novelty_claim: The novelty is to narrow differentiable inference to a human-authored gravity toy, where the main input is an orbit trail rather than a video stream or a control objective.
differentiation: Prior work usually infers physics from perception pipelines or optimizes policies through physics. This concept instead uses a tiny inverse solver as an educational affordance inside the simulator itself.
